chunks: We were told by my father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they both said: We were told by Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, who said: We were told by al-Nadr ibn Shu'aib, from Abdul-Ghaffar al-Jazi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

With regards to the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Allah only wants, verily, to remove from you impurity, (O) Household, and to purify you a (complete) purification.» He said: Impurity is doubt.

key_terms.الرِّجْس: Impurity or filth, here interpreted as doubt

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'Rijs' (impurity) refer to in the verse of Purification according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a distinctive exegetical view by interpreting 'Rijs' (impurity) in the Verse of Purification specifically as 'doubt' (Shakk), rather than general sin or impurity. This interpretation underscores the intellectual and spiritual infallibility of the Ahl al-Bayt, ensuring they are free from uncertainty in their religious authority and teachings. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Ahl al-Bayt's unique status as the pure vessels of divine knowledge.
